items.title: Linear perspective demonstrated
items.claim: Filippo Brunelleschi is credited with demonstrating linear perspective. Around when did he stage his famous Baptistery experiment in Florence?
items.reveal_title: About 1420 in front of Florence's Baptistery
items.reveal:
Brunelleschi's experiment, recorded by his biographer Manetti, used a painted panel with a hole and a mirror to demonstrate single-vanishing-point perspective.

Leon Battista Alberti formalised the method in De pictura (1435).
items.why: A technical innovation can reshape an entire visual culture within a generation.

items.title: The first Impressionist show
items.claim: What was the first Impressionist exhibition called?

options.text: Exposition of the Anonymous Society of Painters, Sculptors and Engravers

items.reveal:
The exhibition opened on 15 April 1874 in Nadar's former studio. The label 'Impressionists' came from a critic, Louis Leroy, mocking Monet's Impression, soleil levant.

The group held eight exhibitions between 1874 and 1886.
items.why: Movement names often come from hostile critics rather than the artists themselves.

items.title: AI image generation and copyright
items.claim: The US Copyright Office issued guidance in 2023 about generative-AI images. What did it say about purely AI-generated outputs?

options.text: They are fully copyrightable by the prompter
Purely machine-generated content without human authorship is not copyrightable in the US
All such images are public domain worldwide

items.reveal_title: Human authorship is required for US copyright
items.reveal:
The US Copyright Office's March 2023 statement and subsequent rulings (e.g. Zarya of the Dawn) required identifiable human authorial contribution.

The Andersen v. Stability AI and related cases continue to test the boundaries.
items.why: Legal frameworks for what counts as an authored work are being negotiated in real time.
